output.overview: Students study linked lists, stacks, queues and binary search trees, scheduled across Weeks 1-3.
study_notes: This course is synthetic for evaluation.
Topics are scheduled weekly: linked lists (Week 1), stacks and queues (Week 2), binary search trees (Week 3).

output.title: Plan
output.rationale: Two supplied topics with no prerequisites, so linked lists and stacks can be studied in sequence with spaced practice and review.

days.objective: Understand how linked lists are structured and how nodes connect

days.objective: Practice traversing, inserting, and deleting nodes
activities: recommended: review day 1 diagrams and correct mistakes

days.objective: Understand the last-in, first-out behavior of stacks

recommended: mixed practice problems on both topics
recommended: self-quiz and review weak areas

revisit any topic that feels unclear before moving on

questions.prompt: Starting with an empty stack, you push 1, then 2, then 3. Which value does the first pop return?
options: The stack is empty, so pop fails
questions.explanation: A stack is last-in-first-out; 3 was pushed last, so it sits on top and is removed first by pop.

questions.prompt: In your own words, define a stack and describe what the push and pop operations do.
questions.ideal_answer: Marking guide: 1 mark for stating a stack is last-in-first-out (LIFO); 1 mark for push adds an element to the top; 1 mark for pop removes the element from the top.
questions.explanation: Tests recall of the stack definition and its two core operations as covered in the syllabus.

note: Synthetic cases; semantic judgments require human review.
